title: Session 3b54e160: A Single-Trajectory Dataset of Shrink-Collapse in an LLM Tool-Use Agent
description:
A fully annotated, single-trajectory dataset of an LLM agent that progressively stopped acting while its tone stayed confident.

What it contains

  • 137 turns / 1,384 assistant steps / 10,816 events, model deepseek-flash
  • Per-step annotations: tool calls, characters, action verbs, assertions, hedges, evidence markers, falsification language, template hits, duplicate share, pseudo-certainty
  • Labels: normal (1,100) / suspect (274) / collapse (10)
  • Full append-only session log, plus every artifact the session produced (111 files)
  • The experimental context: rule files, tools, and the 1,405-character persona block inserted at turn 86, with system-prompt snapshots before and after
  • Reproduction code and a pre/post-T86 statistical analysis

Why it is interesting: existing degeneration work focuses on expansion (one phrase emitted tens of thousands of times). This session shows the opposite: text and actions shrink while assertion density stays flat, so a repetition detector with a calibrated threshold of 0.80 fires zero times (maximum duplicate share observed: 0.44).

Statistical note: the effect size for tool-call density is small at the step level (Cliff's delta 0.144) but medium-to-large at the turn level (0.521), because the step-level variable is discrete and its median saturates. Both are reported.

Scope: one session. It supports existence claims about this failure mode, not prevalence claims. The persona injection is confounded with time and context length; causal attribution requires the control experiment described in docs/CONFOUNDERS.md.
notes: Author GitHub handle: ganaha-HUD. The session log is UTF-8. The compressed log is a concatenation of 5,990 zstd frames; a single-shot decompressor returns only the first frame. An uncompressed copy is included. No credentials or third-party personal data are present (verified by scanning every file).
